CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Raymond reports difficulty swallowing for several weeks with associated chest pain when swallowing. Pain occurs when swallowing most foods, particularly larger pieces that feel stuck. Symptoms are not present with every meal. Patient denies weight loss and states he has actually gained weight. Onset appears related to stress from recent move from west coast to east coast over the last couple of months. During this time, patient reports consuming more unhealthy foods including pizza and burgers. Patient reports some epigastric pain. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stools.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies generalized abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Reports some epigastric discomfort. No blood in stool or dark tarry stools.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is relocating from west coast to east coast. Reports significant stress related to the move, including concerns about transporting his dog. Plans to drive for the relocation. Has been consuming more alcohol and caffeine due to stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 133/70, heart rate normal, afebrile, O2 saturation 100%, respiratory rate 19. Weight gain of 10 pounds over the last month noted. Mouth exam: no obvious ulcers or thrush, tonsils midline. Neck: no adenopathy, no thyromegaly. Abdomen: nondistended, active bowel sounds, pain to palpation of epigastric area noted, negative Murphy's sign, no peritoneal signs, no rebound. Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally. Skin: no rash, lesions, or bruising. Eyes: equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow study revealed two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis. Prescribed Protonix 40 mg once daily in the morning to reduce acid production. Prescribed Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to coat the esophageal and gastric lining. Patient advised to avoid alcohol, caffeine, citrus fruits, and spicy foods until symptoms improve. Counseled to eat slowly and chew food thoroughly. Upper endoscopy scheduled for next week. Follow-up visit next week. Patient encouraged to focus on healthy eating and lifestyle management once settled after relocation.
